summary: After the accepted eat.c:eatmupdate fix, the first mismatch is the small-mimic completion boundary: at step 52 C still has Hallucination and renders the hero as an orange (%), while JavaScript has already cleared Hallucination and renders gold ($). The source cause is the missing blocking C window call in eat.c:cpostfx(): C flushes the mimic glyph and waits at display_nhwindow(WIN_MAP, TRUE) before returning to the turn loop, while js/eat.js skips that call with note_unported and allows nh_timeout() to expire Hallucination one input earlier. The existing TTY helper already models the required pending-message wait.

source.branch: In cpostfx(PM_SMALL_MIMIC), when the hero is not already a mimic and is not Unchanging, C selects ORANGE while Hallucination is active, writes the pending completion message, updates the map, calls curs_on_u(), and blocks at display_nhwindow(WIN_MAP, TRUE). For this recipe the pending You_cant message sets TOPLINE_NEED_MORE, so the TTY map-window implementation enters its WIN_MESSAGE blocking path before cpostfx returns.
callers: eat.c:done_eating() calls cpostfx(piece->corpsenm) for a consumed corpse or globby at line 563; it is reached from eatfood() and doeat(). JavaScript js/eat.js:done_eating() is reached from eatfood() and immediate doeat() completion.
eat.c:consume_tin() calls cpostfx(mnum) after cprefx() when the tin remains at line 1613; JavaScript js/eat.js:consume_tin() follows the same condition.

eat.c:Finish_digestion() calls cpostfx(gc.corpsenm_digested) at line 3964; uhitm.c:gulpum() sets gc.corpsenm_digested and ga.afternmv=Finish_digestion, then hack.c:unmul() invokes the callback. JavaScript js/uhitm.js:gulpum() stores the species and Finish_digestion callback, and js/hack.js:unmul() invokes it.
dependencies: C display.c:curs_on_u() calls flush_screen(1) before placing the cursor; JavaScript js/eat.js awaits js/hack.js:curs_on_u(), which performs the map flush.

C win/tty/wintty.c:tty_display_nhwindow() handles NHW_MAP with blocking=true by ending glyph output, marking a pending topline TOPLINE_NEED_MORE, and recursively calling tty_display_nhwindow(WIN_MESSAGE, TRUE). JavaScript js/tty_message.js:displayPendingTtyMessageWindow() already waits for a pending TTY message and retires that window in C order.
eat.c:cpostfx() also calls steed.c:dismount_steed() with its result discarded; the existing allowed note_unported skip remains unrelated to this non-mounted mismatch.
source.javascriptGap: js/eat.js:cpostfx() performs the same mimic setup and map flush, then calls note_unported('windows.c display_nhwindow') and returns. The skipped blocking wait lets the enclosing turn proceed to timeout processing before the C path does. Replace that skip with the existing displayPendingTtyMessageWindow(state) call after curs_on_u(state); no shared TTY implementation change is needed.

proposedImplementationScope.entryPointEvidence: Use the admitted v47 case through the normal corpse/done_eating path for the timed mimic boundary, the existing mimic-tin recordings for consume_tin, and a recorded gulpum purple-worm case for Finish_digestion. Verify all cited existing recordings strictly after the change; create a fresh recipe/recording only if an entry point lacks a matching existing record.

evidence: Current saved queue entry and accepted evaluation challenges/evaluations/accepted-bbed9236788ed585d4a6bfe887bb307954dff29d-v47.json identify a single screen mismatch at zero-based segment 0, step 52: C cell (row 5, column 28) is (% , color 9); JS cell is ($, color 11). RNG (2667/2667) and cursors (54/54) match; 53/54 screens match.

The raw C boundary in challenges/cases/v47/v47-mimic-hallucination-timeout-eatmupdate-attempt11-clean-cfirst.session.json shows Hallu still set and the hero rendered as ORANGE at step 52, then Hallu clears at step 53. A fresh JS replay of the same input shows Hallu already cleared at step 52 and the hero rendered as GOLD.

Upstream eat.c:cpostfx() lines 1129-1328 (mimic arm 1173-1226) sets the mimic message and appearance, calls newsym(), calls curs_on_u(), then display_nhwindow(WIN_MAP, TRUE). Upstream win/tty/wintty.c:tty_display_nhwindow() lines 1855-1890 blocks the NHW_MAP route on a nonempty topline by setting TOPLINE_NEED_MORE and calling the blocking WIN_MESSAGE route.

The current js/eat.js:cpostfx() line 2764 instead calls note_unported('windows.c display_nhwindow') after curs_on_u(). js/hack.js:curs_on_u() flushes the map; js/tty_message.js:displayPendingTtyMessageWindow() implements the pending WIN_MESSAGE blocking wait that the C map-window route delegates to.

The three direct C callers are eat.c:done_eating() line 563, eat.c:consume_tin() line 1613, and eat.c:Finish_digestion() line 3964. The last is scheduled by uhitm.c:gulpum() lines 5091-5092 and invoked by hack.c:unmul() after clearing ga.afternmv. Their JavaScript call paths are already wired in js/eat.js/js/uhitm.js/js/hack.js.
